$comment: EDE-105 (approved on EDE-94): THE CHAT STORE, one Rust crate for every client (apps/desktop/crates/chat-store: a pure core + a SQLite adapter, no async runtime in the core) that keeps every chat on every device, offline, opened from disk, plus a local search index. This TS reference (src/chat-store.ts) and the crate (its in-memory core AND its SQLite adapter) replay every case below. WHAT IT HOLDS, per account (desktop: `{data_dir}/accounts/<account>/chat-store.sqlite`, beside the sync store, kept across a session expiry and an account switch, deleted by a deliberate sign-out (SIGN-OUT below), gone with the account's data): (1) the synced `messages` rows of every chat the member can see (the `messages` shape's own visibility rule), OPENED with the chat key (EXP-1459, `sealed-content.json`); a row whose key is not held yet is stored with `body: null`, never indexed, and replaced (latest wins, by id) once the key arrives and it opens; (2) the TRANSCRIPT EVENTS of every session of those chats (the wire `activity` events with their seq, exactly as on the wire: already scrubbed by the emitter, never more than a viewer sees), with `rootId`, `sessionId`, `deviceId` (the device that ran it), `seq` and `storedAt` (ms the store took it). TRANSCRIPTS NEVER TOUCH THE SERVER: events reach a store only from the device running the session or another reader device, over eNet (steer-enet.json); the server keeps carrying the messages only. DECRYPTED ONLY WHERE THE PLATFORM STORE IS PROTECTED: desktop = the per-account data dir, user-only (0600 file, like the journal and the keyring); iOS = Data Protection (complete until first unlock) in the app container; Android = app-private storage; web = OPFS (origin-private). A platform without a protected store keeps the bodies sealed as synced and indexes nothing sealed. DEDUP: an event is keyed by (sessionId, deviceId, seq): the first write wins, a repeat (a history page overlapping the live feed, a second reader answering the same page) is dropped; a session moved in place (session-device-move.json) restarts its seqs on its new device, so each device's events are their own sequence; events read back per session and device in seq order (`ingest.cases`). INDEX SCOPE (`docs`): user inputs (`user_message`), narration, tool titles (`name` + ` ` + `detail`, or `name`), tool output as on the wire (`tool_update` `output`, else its `diff`; the hit lands on the tool's row: the lowest seq of a `tool` with that id in the session on that device, else the update's own seq) and synced message bodies (`message`); NEVER thoughts, never slots (usage, config, diff snapshots) or card payloads. A doc's time = the event's `at`, else `storedAt` (a message: `createdAt`). QUERY SEMANTICS = steer-enet.json SEARCH (find in chat, EDE-96): a case- and diacritics-insensitive LITERAL: the query and the text collapse every run of ASCII whitespace to one space (trimmed), fold per code point (NFD, marks dropped, lowercased), the query keeps its first `queryMaxChars` code points, an empty query searches nothing; one hit per doc (its first match; an event's hit names its `deviceId` and `seq`, a message's its `messageId`), `snippet` = the collapsed text from `snippetLeadChars` before the match, `snippetChars` wide (more only for a longer match), `…` where cut, `matchStart`/`matchLen` in code points of the snippet. DEDUP OF HITS: a `message` hit whose collapsed body equals a `user_message`/`narration` hit's text in the same session is dropped (the final reply and the person's input exist twice; the transcript row is the one a reader lands on). ORDER: newest first by time, then session id ascending, then device id ascending, then seq descending (a message, without a seq, after the events of the same instant), then message id. FIND IN CHAT (`search.chatCases`): one chat (`rootId`, every session of its tree), at most `limit` hits (clamped to [1, hitsMax]), `total` = every hit. GLOBAL (`search.allCases`, S5): one row per chat {rootId, count, hit = its newest hit}, newest chat first, at most `limit` rows, `total` = chats matched. OPEN: a chat opens from the store before any live feed attaches: per session, the stored events of the device it is on now through the same REPLAY TAIL rule a join replays by (steer-enet.json), older ones paged from the store; the live feed's `activity_reset` replay then replaces the seed and everything it carries is stored as it arrives. RETENTION (`retention`): per form factor (`constants.retentionDays`): desktop keeps everything (null); phones and web keep prose (inputs, narration) and every synced message forever and every other event (tool steps, their output, slots) for the last `retentionDays` days by its time (the cutoff instant kept); a storage setting changes the window; an older tool step is fetched over eNet when its chat is opened (S2). PHASES: S1 = this spec + the crate + desktop (the store fed from the device's own journals, the synced messages and every feed the desktop views; a chat opens from it). S2 = background catch-up over eNet (`catchUp`, #EDE-108): a reader asks the running device or ANY reader device holding the events (its store answers a device-naming `history_page` like a journal does; the EDE-96 `search` frame follows) for every seq it lacks, deduped by seq. S3 = phones through `exponential-mobile-ffi` (the same crate; iOS + Android retention 30 days). S4 = web through wasm with the store in OPFS (#EDE-115: crate chat-store-wasm, loaded lazily in a worker, never the main bundle): ONE APPEND-ONLY LOG per chat (`chat-store/<user>/<rootId>.log`, a generation line first) opened through a sync access handle under a Web Lock per file, so every tab's worker shares it; a write appends only what changed (events deduped as above, messages latest wins except that a body that did not open in this browser never replaces one that did: a tab without the key yet); RETENTION (`retentionDays.web`) applies when a worker first opens a chat and rewrites the file under a new generation; fed from every steer feed a view receives and the synced messages a chat loads (web messages are on demand); the catch-up asks and answers (`catchUp`, `minAt` = its cutoff) only in the tab holding the eNet node's Web Lock; OPEN paints the stored tail before the dial (its live slots `turn`, `queue`, `rate_limit`, `background_tasks` left out: a stored one may be a finished run's), and older pages come from the store while no feed is open; signing out stops it in every tab and deletes the account's files (SIGN-OUT). SIGN-OUT (`signOut`, #EDE-120, decided on #EDE-94: the store holds chats DECRYPTED): leaving an account (`reason`) DELETES its store files only on a DELIBERATE sign-out (`sign_out`: the person's Sign out on desktop or web, or the CLI's `logout`, which shares the desktop's data dir), after STOPPING the store (desktop: the writer thread, the catch-up loop and the store this device serves pages from, the files going once every holder let go; web: the worker in EVERY tab, told over the `exp-chat-store` BroadcastChannel, which also leaves the catch-up without a store); a session expiry or a lost token (`expired`) and an account switch (`switch`) delete nothing, the files stay for the next sign-in. The files are picked from a listing (paths relative to the data dir or the OPFS root): desktop `accounts/<account>/chat-store.sqlite` and its `-wal`, `-shm`, `-journal` siblings; web every file directly in `chat-store/<account>/` (its logs; the store keeps no subdirectories, and the emptied dir goes too); never anything else of the account (its sync store stays, like a sign-out leaves it) and never another account's (segment-exact: `u1` never matches `u10`); an account id that is not one safe path segment (1 to 255 of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, never all dots: `.` and `..` are not segments, never a separator) deletes nothing. REAL ACCOUNT NAMES (#EDE-120 follow-up): the desktop's account dirs are `<host>--<userId>` with the host's dots kept and every other character (a port's `:`) turned into `-` (api `account_id_for`: `app.exponential.at--8Jk3…`, `localhost-3000--u1`); the cases use those shapes, not only bare ids. A delete that fails (a file still held) is tried again a few times and otherwise left: the sign-out itself never waits on it. S5 = the Chats section in global search (EDE-99) reading `searchAll`.

catchUp.$comment: #EDE-108 S2 BACKGROUND CATCH-UP (desktop + CLI first; phones S3 and the web S4 speak the same frames). Transcripts travel DEVICE TO DEVICE over eNet only (never the server, never the sealed relay tunnel: a catch-up page arriving on a tunnel is ignored). WHAT: for every chat the account can read (every synced `sessions` row with a `deviceId` that is not this device: this device's own runs are fed by its journals, S1), a reader keeps per (sessionId, deviceId = the device the session is on now) a `completeTo` watermark (the seq through which it holds every event that exists; absent = none), in the store's own bookkeeping, so a walk RESUMES after a restart where it stopped. THE WIRE (steer-enet.json's envelope, unchanged): the ask is a `history_page` that names a device: `{t:"history_page", requestId, deviceId, afterSeq?, limit, have, minAt?}` (absent `afterSeq` = from the first seq; `have` = the RUNS of seqs the asker already holds above `afterSeq`, `haveRuns`, at most `haveRunsMax`, the lowest first; `minAt` = the asker's RETENTION cutoff, phones and web only). It needs no `join` and is answered to the asker only with ONE `history_chunk {requestId, deviceId, events, seqs, done, throughSeq, lastSeq, fullTo}`, or the same chunk empty with `error` (`unauthorized`, `no_such_session`): never the feed's `error` frame (it would end a viewer's feed of the same session). A `history_page` without `deviceId` is a viewer's page as before. A build that does not know the form ignores it (the asker's `askTimeoutMs` moves on). THE HOLDER (any device, under the SAME access rule as a join: the session's synced row on the holder, the asker's user from the session team's registry list, `viewer_allowed`; no row = `no_such_session`): the device the session is on answers off its JOURNAL (every event of the file, `read_journal_seq`, slots included: the store keeps the wire) with `fullTo` = its last seq (the journal is the whole record); any other device (or a runner without the file) answers off its CHAT STORE with `fullTo` = its own `completeTo` for that (session, device) (a store fed by live feeds and pages holds holes); a device holding neither answers an empty chunk. ANSWER (`answerCases`: `events` are {seq, kind, at}, `eventRange` [first, last] = narration at 0 for every seq between; `limit` clamped to [1, `pageMax`]): scanning its events above `afterSeq` in seq order, skipping every seq inside a `have` run and (with `minAt`) every non-prose event whose time (`at`, else `storedAt`) is before it, it takes the first `limit`; `throughSeq` = the last taken when the page is full, else the larger of `afterSeq` and its `lastSeq` (absent when both are); `done` = it holds nothing above `throughSeq`. A page over one envelope (steer-enet.json `chatMaxBytes`, less a margin) is cut from its end (`throughSeq` = the last kept, `done` false); an event too large alone is skipped (`throughSeq` = its seq). THE ASKER: PROGRESS (`progressCases`): `reach` = min(`throughSeq`, `fullTo`) (none when either is absent); when the asker was complete through the page's `afterSeq` (none counts as below every seq) and `reach` is above its `completeTo`, `completeTo` = `reach`; the next ask's `afterSeq` = `throughSeq` until `done`. Every event received is stored (DEDUP by (session, device, seq), `ingest`) with the asker's `rootId` and the ask's `deviceId`, whether or not it advanced the watermark. HOLDERS (`holderCases`): the installs of the session's device (the runner: `deviceId` equal) newest `lastSeenAt` first, then the asker's OWN other installs newest first (phones too); never itself, never a teammate's device (they serve, under the rule, but only the asker's own devices spend their bandwidth for it); an endpoint that timed out or refused is skipped for `endpointBackoffMs`. WALK (`walkCases`): per holder in order, pages from `completeTo` until `done`; the session is CAUGHT UP once a RUNNER's walk ends complete through its `lastSeq` (then no later holder is asked); readers only fill in, so a session served by readers alone is retried (`retryCases`: `passIntervalMs` × 2^attempts, at most `retryMaxMs`). A caught-up session is skipped until its synced row changes (`updatedAt`); a `busy` one is walked every pass. BOUNDS: at most `concurrency` sessions walk at once, newest chat first (the row's `updatedAt`); pages pass a TOKEN BUCKET (`bucketCases`: `bytesPerSecond`, capacity `burstBytes`, starting full; an answer's bytes are spent when it arrives, the next ask waits until the balance is back to zero: wait = ceil(debt × 1000 / rate) ms; refill = floor(elapsed × rate / 1000)); POWER (`gateCases`): on battery (when the platform tells) a pass runs only once the person has been idle `idleAfterMs` (desktop: no app window active), on mains or unknown always. A pass runs every `passIntervalMs` and at once when the account's sessions change.
